claims.claim: A typical Laravel endpoint that runs a few Eloquent queries handles roughly 100–200 requests a second on 2 vCPUs
claims.measured: php-laravel on 1 CPU: 149 req/s for one DB query, 93 req/s for 20 queries; roughly 190–300 req/s on 2 vCPUs
claims.why: For a few queries the measurements suggest about 200–250 req/s on 2 vCPUs, which is within a factor of 2 of the claimed 100–200.
Every server was already tuned for production, so there is no untuned-vs-tuned Laravel comparison.

claims.claim: A Go or Node rewrite might be 5–10 times faster per request
claims.about: Go (Gin, net/http) and Node (Express, Fastify) vs php-laravel
claims.measured: One DB query: go-gin 22,138 and node-express 9,034 vs php-laravel 149 (about 150x and 60x). 20 queries: 2,535 and 1,062 vs 93 (about 27x and 11x). Plaintext: 53,941 and 17,601 vs 681 (about 79x and 26x)
claims.why: In almost every test Go and Node measured far more than 2 times faster than the claimed 5–10x; only Express on the 20-query test comes near 10x.

claims.claim: A Go or Node rewrite still wouldn't be enough on this (2 vCPU) server to reach 3,000 req/s
claims.measured: go-gin on 1 CPU: 22,138 req/s with one DB query, 2,535 with 20 queries; node-express: 9,034 and 1,062
claims.why: Scaled to 2 vCPUs, Go reaches about 44,000 req/s on a single-query endpoint and about 5,000 even with 20 queries, so 3,000 is well within reach.

claims.claim: Laravel Octane keeps the framework loaded between requests and is 2–5 times faster
claims.measured: Plaintext 1,172 vs 681 (1.7x), JSON 1.7x, CPU 1.5x, one DB query 732 vs 149 (4.9x), 20 queries 1.3x; I/O wait 86 vs 591 (slower)
claims.why: Most tests measured a 1.3–4.9x speed-up, within a factor of 2 of the claimed 2–5x, though Octane was much slower in the I/O-wait test.

claims.claim: Octane can leak memory between requests
claims.measured: Peak memory about 100–116 MB vs 58–75 MB for FPM Laravel; idle 94 MB
claims.why: Octane does use more memory, but 15 s runs can't show whether memory grows over time.

claims.claim: Serving 3,000 uncached Laravel requests a second needs a lot of hardware
claims.measured: php-laravel on 1 CPU: 149 req/s with one DB query, 681 plaintext
claims.why: At about 150–700 req/s per core, 3,000 req/s needs roughly 5–20 cores at the server's full rate, and more to leave headroom.

claims.claim: If 5% of the 3,000 req/s is per-user it's easy; if 40% you need several servers
claims.measured: php-laravel 149 req/s per CPU with one DB query (about 300 on 2 vCPUs)
claims.why: 150 req/s fits on one 2 vCPU server, while 1,200 req/s needs about 8 cores, i.e. several 2 vCPU servers.
